2004–05 was the first season of the [[New Zealand Football Championship]], replacing the [[New Zealand National Football Leagues]], which ran from 1970 to 2003. It was organised by the [[New Zealand Football]] and was contested by eight competing teams.

==Season summary==
The league kicked off on 15 October 2004, with a 3–1 victory for [[Auckland City FC|Auckland City]] at [[Napier City Rovers]] and it soon became clear that Auckland City, along with [[Waitakere United]], were the class teams in the championship. Auckland lost only three games all year en route to becoming the first winners of the [[New Zealand Football Championship]], while Waitakere lost four times to Auckland City, including the thrilling 3–2 final in front of 3,800 spectators at Auckland City's home field, [[Kiwitea Street]], where Auckland came back from 2-1 down to win in the last minutes of the game.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesn/nz05.html |title=New Zealand 2004/05 |publisher=[[RSSSF]] |date=28 September 2005 |access-date=11 June 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://aucklandcityfc.com/about/default.asp |title=Auckland City Football Club |website=aucklandcityfc.com |access-date=11 June 2025 |archive-date=22 December 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151222192534/http://aucklandcityfc.com/about/default.asp |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Waikato FC came out best of the rest to take the final playoff position in third, despite making a slow start to the season. Notables among the other teams were Napier City Rovers, who also came back from a slow start to have a chance of making the playoffs in the final week of the season. Otago United won five games all year, but did not win any of their last twelve games.

==Oceania Club Championship==
By winning the NZFC, Auckland City went on to represent New Zealand in the [[OFC Men's Champions League|Oceania Club Championship]] in Tahiti. Auckland lost their first game to [[Australians|Australian]] representatives [[Sydney FC]], 3–2 in the dying minutes. Their next game, against tournament hosts [[AS Pirae]] of [[Tahiti]], was also a loss, this time by 1–0. Auckland City would take some consolation from finishing third in their group after defeating the champions of [[Papua New Guinea]], [[Sobou FC]], by 6–1.
